card.name: Subject right before "should"
card.fires_on: The last word of a subject noun phrase, just before the verb "should" or "can" in a label instruction. It is often a pronoun such as they or it, or the end of a patient or drug name.

modes.label: Pronoun subject
modes.description: A pronoun such as they or it that refers back to patients, shoes, or products and is followed by should.
modes.example: that if they feel dizzy or light-headed after taking Moxidectin Tablets,<< they>> should lie down until the symptoms resolve.

modes.label: End of a patient or drug noun phrase
modes.description: The last piece of a drug or patient-group name that serves as the subject of a coming "should" instruction.
modes.example: Patients receiving a GnRH agon<<ist>> should be monitored for symptoms and signs suggestive

card.writes: It suppresses must and must-like words in several languages, so the model favors a softer verb such as should.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a subject is about to be followed by "should" in advice, not "must".
